How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to **generate a RESTful API request** for the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1**.  
I’ll walk you through the UI flow, then give you ready‑to‑copy snippets for both `cURL` and Python (`requests`). Finally I’ll show how you can invoke the built‑in `functions.requests_get` helper if you’re working inside a script that already has that wrapper available.

---

## 1️⃣  Log In & Open the API Explorer

| Step | What to do | Screenshot hint |
|------|------------|------------------|
| 1 | Sign in to your Cisco Nexus Dashboard account. | – |
| 2 | From the left‑hand navigation pane, click **Developer** → **API Explorer**. | ![API Explorer](https://example.com/api-explorer.png) |

> **Tip:** If you don’t see “Developer”, you may need to enable the *Developer* role in your organization’s settings.

---

## 2️⃣  Pick the Right API Version

| Step | What to do | Screenshot hint |
|------|------------|------------------|
| 1 | At the top of the page, there’s a drop‑down labeled **API Version**. Choose **6.3.1**. | ![API Version](https://example.com/api-version.png) |
| 2 | The list of endpoints will refresh to match that version. | – |

---

## 3️⃣  Locate the Endpoint

| Step | What to do | Screenshot hint |
|------|------------|------------------|
| 1 | Search for “device connector versions” in the search bar or scroll until you find the **Device Connector Versions** group. | ![Endpoint Group](https://example.com/endpoint-group.png) |
| 2 | Expand the group; you’ll see the **GET /device_connector_versions** operation. | ![Operation](https://example.com/get-operation.png) |

---

## 4️⃣  Generate the Request

| Step | What to do | Screenshot hint |
|------|------------|------------------|
| 1 | Click the **Generate Request** button next to the operation. | ![Generate Request](https://example.com/generate-request.png) |
| 2 | A modal pops up showing the raw request template. | – |
| 3 | Fill in any required path/query/body parameters. For this endpoint you typically only need an optional `device_id` filter. | ![Fill Parameters](https://example.com/fill-parameters.png) |
| 4 | Click **Copy** to copy the generated request to your clipboard. | – |

---

## 5️⃣  Execute the Request

### 5.1 Using `cURL`

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://nexus-dashboard.cisco.com/api/v6.3.1/device_connector_versions?device_id=12345" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

Replace:

- `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` with a valid OAuth bearer token.
- `12345` with the ID of the device you’re querying (omit the query string entirely if you want all connectors).

### 5.2 Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://nexus-dashboard.cisco.com/api/v6.3.1"
ENDPOINT = "/device_connector_versions"

headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN",
    "Accept": "application/json",
}

params = {
    # Uncomment and set if you want to filter by device
    # "device_id": "12345"
}

resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}{ENDPOINT}", headers=headers, params=params)

if resp.ok:
    data = resp.json()
    print("Connector Versions:")
    for item in data.get("results", []):
        print(f"- {item['name']} (v{item['version']})")
else:
    print(f"Error {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}")
```

> **Note:** The `results` key is typical for paginated responses; adjust according to the actual schema returned by your instance.

---

## 6️⃣  Using the Built‑In Helper (`functions.requests_get`)

If you’re writing a script that already imports the `functions` namespace, you can skip the manual `requests` import and just call the helper:

```python
from functions import requests_get

result = requests_get({
    "url": "https://nexus-dashboard.cisco.com/api/v6.3.1/device_connector_versions",
    "params": {"device_id": "12345"},   # Omit or comment out if not needed
})

print(result)   # This will contain the parsed JSON response
```

The helper automatically handles:

- Adding the `Authorization` header (you’ll still need to supply the token via environment variable or config).
- Parsing the JSON body into a Python dict.
- Raising exceptions on non‑200 status codes.

---

## 7️⃣  Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Verify that the bearer token is fresh and has the `read:device_connector_versions` scope. |
| **404 Not Found** | Double‑check the base URL (`https://nexus-dashboard.cisco.com`) and that you’re using the correct API version (`/api/v6.3.1`). |
| **Empty results** | Ensure you’re passing a valid `device_id`. If omitted, the endpoint returns all connectors but may paginate; check the `next` link in the response. |
| **Rate limiting (429)** | Add exponential back‑off or reduce request frequency. |

---

## 8️⃣  Quick Reference Cheat Sheet

| Item | Example |
|------|---------|
| Base URL | `https://nexus-dashboard.cisco.com/api/v6.3.1` |
| Endpoint | `/device_connector_versions` |
| Full URL (with filter) | `https://nexus-dashboard.cisco.com/api/v6.3.1/device_connector_versions?device_id=12345` |
| Required Header | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| Accept Header | `Accept: application/json` |

---

### 🎉 You’re All Set!

Now you can programmatically pull the latest connector version info for any device in your Nexus Dashboard environment. Happy coding!
